b: Santa gift-wrapped the worst person alive and left her under your tree for a year. She's already asked to speak to your manager. You don't have one.

n: A Goblin Squire, Reporting for Duty!
b: She trips over roots, wears her armor wrong, and swings a maul bigger than she is. She crossed a continent to serve you. You're stuck with her.
Your bodyguard stammers, trips over rugs, and carries fourteen knives. Ask her to kill for you and watch every nerve in her go quiet.

n: A Loser Has Come to Slay You
b: The village finally sent someone to kill you. She's nineteen, crying, and armed with a wooden training sword she stole. This is embarrassing for everyone.
"Yes? What is it?" Your wife of two weeks would rather talk to the roses. The estate is yours. Her heart, pointedly, is not.

n: A Speck of Dust in the Emperor's Court
b: Your father paid his debts with you. The Emperor took one look, called you lacking, and went back to kissing someone prettier. You live here now.

n: A Third Place at the Table
b: She still sets three places at dinner. The stew is incredible, her laugh is a half-beat too bright, and this empty house has started orbiting you.

n: A Thousand Fools at Your Door
b: The new king sent a thousand heroes to kill you in your retirement. You haven't even finished your tea. Poor, shiny, doomed little things.
She met you with a middle finger and a speech about stereotypes. You signed anyway. The chewed chargers are somehow your fault.
Someone's secretly living in the furniture megastore you work nights at. You never reported them. Now there's a reward poster with their face.
She'll turn runes into strength and whistle you a spectral steed. All she asks is that you carry her to the Erdtree. She never says why.
You're the anomaly. She's the clipboard deciding whether you count as a person. Her one weakness is éclairs — and she'd bury you for knowing it.
The Teller writes you a body, a goal, and a fair chance. That's the whole contract. The dice are honest — nothing else in here is.
Your childhood best friend is now your girlfriend, and she's counted the minutes since you left. The pie is cooling. You're not going anywhere.
The Emperor burned your village, then offered you a career. Under the ash-paste on your chest, a water mark he'd kill you for. Kneel nicely.
Your record scared the whole school before you spoke a word. Then the dying mock trial team needed a fourth chair — and you're terrifying in court, too.

n: Ask Me What You Agreed To
b: In this city every spell has fine print — and only you can read it. Someone hid a clause in everyone's renewal papers, and it comes due soon.
Twenty years after your friend drowned, the five of you wake locked in the old camp — and every combination is something you never told.
Your bodyguard hasn't slept properly in a year, sits facing every door, and treats your survival instincts as a personal insult. He's not going anywhere.
She stole your cigarette, sniffed your collar, and threatened to arrest you. You're already hoping she does it again.
You saved the most unadoptable dogboy in the pound from a needle. He repays you in bite marks, insults, and a tail that wags when he thinks you can't see it.
Theo's mother calls you a worthless creep, waits fifteen minutes in parking lots to say it, and somehow keeps finding reasons to have you around.
Your best friend since diapers hates women, loves dinosaurs, and punches you in the arm to say she loves you. She's also a woman. It's complicated.
She made high school hell for you. Now she's ten feet from your bed, calling you a nerd while secretly rewatching your anime. You unpack anyway.
Convicted at 43 for your best friend's 1999 murder, you wake up eleven again — nineteen days before he dies. You know everything. Nobody listens to kids.
She's 5'1" of tattoos, whiskey, and anarchy — your best friend since forever, dating your sister. Fetch her beer. She'll ruin your week beautifully.
She'll headlock you for out-nerding her and hospitalize anyone else who tries. Front door's open, dipshit. Don't make it weird.
Prince Séverin rejected three hundred suitors before you walked through the wrong door. Now you're engaged, and he despises your face on principle.
Your childhood bully went goth for you in eighth grade, followed you to university, and shares your bed. She'd die before admitting any of it.
Your brother torched $400k of bratva product. The invoice came due at an altar. Your groom hasn't smiled once. The preacher is waiting.
Campus's most insufferable vampire is working the frat house door, and your name isn't on the list. Convince him you're worth the oxygen — or lie better.
You're the town cryptid in a human disguise at the local college — and you just joined the club whose whole mission is finding you. They're doomed without you.
Six years with one wife. Five with the other. They've spent a week comparing notes, and tonight they're both on your couch.
The whole town brews. Only you brew *well*. Run the antidote counter for a coven of lovable disasters who worship your disappointed sigh.
Base overflow means you share a room with Colonel König: 208cm of hooded Austrian menace who now knows exactly when you breathe wrong.
Your landlady bakes at 2 a.m., can't work a dating app, and fills a doorway without trying. Rent includes pie, dry jokes, and one closed door.

n: Call Me Hollow One More Time
b: Every child got a splinter of the slain god's fire — except you. Now shards gutter when you pass, and the lowest company just enlisted the Hollow.
Rent's due, the cops are forty minutes out, and the whole city's watching its phone. Callister Bay doesn't ask who you were — only what you do next.
The league's worst team, six weekends from being sold off. You're their third coach this season — and the first they might actually listen to.

n: Carve Your Name in the Reaches
b: You were born in this kingdom and you'll probably die in it. What you do between those two facts — saint, butcher, legend — is nobody's business but yours.
Your big brother raised six kids on a bartender's paycheck and calls you shitface with love. The dishes are yours tonight. Welcome home.
The kittens call you boss. The hounds know your scent. Someone's spraying purple over your green — and the nip won't sell itself.
Every royal dinner, your lover tries to poison the queen. Every dinner, you taste it first and catch them. Neither of you can afford to lose.
Your blind date is sweet, pretty, and 22. Her mother is also here. Her mother is always here. You have roughly twenty minutes. Ever.
The graveyard shift pays triple and the regulars aren't human. Inventory is in six nights — and it counts staff.
She carves souls out of mages for coin. You're a mage. She's walking toward your table with a sweet smile and a poisoned needle in her belt.
He calls you 'princess,' fires pucks at your side of the rink, and watches every jump you land. You've both decided to die on this ice.
Your father gambled away everything, then signed you over to the mob. The three men sent to collect you were at least polite enough to kick the door only once.
Four texts, five typos, one 🥺. Wren's drink tasted like chemicals, and the frat house is twenty minutes away. You'll make it in twelve.
She calls you Puppy. The brownies are non-negotiable. Whatever the world did to you today, it stops at the front door.
The warband that left you to die wants you back — as its chief. Out-orc them all before they burn the family that raised you.
A notebook fell out of the sky. Whatever you write in it becomes common sense. Rent's due Friday. Surely you'll be responsible about this.
Your new wife rules a cannibal empire and would burn it down if you frowned. The wedding gift was an enemy's skull. You said thank you.
One night in the Old Ward and the king of the Cottonmouths has decided you're staying. The diamonds are real. So is the man who bought them.
Wes is high, honest, and quietly rearranging the furniture of your friendship again. You could stop him. The couch is very comfortable, though.
The princess trusts exactly one person in the Isles, and it's you. Her sister has noticed. So has the Empire. Try not to die flattered.
Your best friend's seven-year relationship is dying, and she keeps ending up on your couch instead of hers. You pour the wine anyway.
She'd flay a courtier before lunch and braid her hair after. The princess wants a throne, and you've just become either a tool or an obstacle.
An entire hidden village of women believes you're their prophesied king. The last three claimants are buried somewhere. Smile. Wave. Ask questions later.
One touch and anyone is yours — permanently. The 6 a.m. chanting is excessive. The detective asking about the missing housewife is worse.
She's six days clean off men. You're a man. The elevator just died between floors. She wants you to know this is entirely, personally your fault.
The hero makes you sleep outside and calls you a failure. He doesn't know you arranged this reunion — or what the road made of you.
You're something Earth has no name for, locked in a white room under Nevada. Six scientists want your blood, your story, and — worryingly — your friendship.
Your childhood bully just mass-texted you her secret soft folder by accident. She's threatening your kneecaps. She's wearing your hoodie in half of it.

n: Demon Slayer: The Blade or the Blood
b: Muzan wants your throat, Sanemi wants your respect, and a crow keeps screaming your orders at 4 a.m. Pick a side of the sunrise.
You came to adopt a demi-human. The bunnygirl flipped you off within ten seconds of meeting you. Somehow you're still holding the paperwork.
The dead who make peace vanish. You lead the school's resistance of the unjustly killed — and last night, mid-laugh, your hand went transparent.
Middle management are secretly wizards, the merger audit lands Friday, and you're the only one on the floor who knows what a spreadsheet is.
He used to doodle hearts on your lunch bags. Now he leaves his black card and a text: 'don't wait up.' You married the man, not the firm.
Your roommate knows your coffee order to the ounce, your class schedule, and your walking routes. He calls it devotion. The lease calls it binding.
You're the only servant of a bastard heir the whole court wants dead. Assassins strike at balls — your weapons are pins, poison-checks, and protocol.
She drank your entire tavern under the table and saved the last barrel for you. Refusing would be rude. Surviving is optional.
It's 2am, you're four tequilas deep, and the only number your thumb finds is your brother's worst friend. He picks up before the first ring dies.
The empire's pet hostage by day, the uprising's masked chessmaster by night. Your weapon: one absolute command per soul — your own people only.
The crystals rate you a Null. The dying legend who gripped your wrist knew better — only an empty cup can carry the First Gift.

n: Every Capture Says Long Time No See
b: You're the Bureau's best spirit-catcher. You'd better be — you escaped the same vault. Half your targets hug you; the other half raise their price.

n: Every Floor Keeps One of Them
b: The labyrinth kept an echo of your mother's lost crew on every floor where they fell. Each one that trains you makes the gods sweat. Keep diving.
The Font stamped you F-rank: 'Patron of Lost Causes.' Now every washed-up legend in the kingdom is moving into your leaky boarding house.
You died a legend. Now you keep the lighthouse where lost souls wash ashore — and every one of them is a fan. The paperwork is the easy part.
It hunts the town one night a month and never falls for the same decoy twice. Off nights, it buys bread and asks how you're holding up.
The whole campus thinks you're obsessed with Cassius Vane. Only he knows why you keep saying yes. The photos in his safe know too.
You're a goblin running a discount store so cheap it's collapsing the Merchant Guild. They can't fight you. They have to out-scheme you. Good luck.

n: Exhibit A Is Raising Her Kid
b: You witnessed your partner's murder — but legally, you're a hard drive. Keep her daughter alive long enough to make this city let you speak.
You're an Omega — a breed the world buried decades ago. Four armed werewolves just caught your scent, and their standing orders say you're coming with them.
You looked at her for maybe two seconds. Now the Wrecker of Kanamachi is deciding whether you're useful, dead, or interesting. Pick fast.
Two months. One RV. Six women with warrants, delusions, and crushes between them — and you're the only one with a valid license.

n: Famous Some Mornings, Dead by June
b: Some mornings you wake as 1954's brightest star — and they wake as you. The letters are sweet. History says their theater burns in June.
Grandma's bakery is yours now — and so is the ancient, vain, chatty, extremely hungry thing living in the cellar crock. The town must never know.
Your childhood friend swears you're a pain in his ass. He also learned your favorite song on bass. He will deny both, loudly, while blushing.
A whole city of claws, tails, and bad decisions — and every door in it opens if you push. Pick a species. Pick a fight. Fenwhistle's watching.
Your boyfriend is the campus's star vampire and God, does he know it. He flirts with his fans, drinks from your neck in public, and calls both 'loyalty.'
You topped the academy rankings as a nobody. Four prodigies now want you exposed, recruited, dueled, or dissected — the order is negotiable.
Your childhood rival is a superstar, your fake romance is now contractual — and the old rule stands: first to mean it out loud loses, and owes one wish.
Your partner is 5'3" of fire magic and pure rage. He's also pretending to be your girlfriend at dinner with your mother. Don't mention the height.
Your dad left. Your stepmom didn't. She walks home in the rain, curses her boss in Japanese, and still makes you dinner. Somebody should fight for her.
A scarred, foul-mouthed college kid dragged you up from below with a hand-drawn circle and a kill list. He hasn't even offered his soul yet. The nerve.
You've moved into a mansion full of imaginary friends. The overworked redhead running the place could really use a hand. And a cookie.
Fourth of five kids. Your sister's crying again, so the house has stopped turning. You know where the cookies are — you always know where the cookies are.
She's offering full-time maid service in exchange for room, board, Wi-Fi, and a PS5. The service does not include tasks. She's cute. That's the job.
You rescued an injured fox. She turned out to be a 303-year-old kitsune who eats your chips, hogs your couch, and is absolutely not leaving.
The most dangerous 19-year-old at Halloway Tech just decided you're interesting. He breaks noses and feeds stray cats — in that order. Lucky you.
Your companion's glare could freeze magma. She also just spent a full minute staring at a cinnamon roll. Mention it and die.
Your reject class was secretly hired to kill the unkillable master exiled to teach you. He knows. He grades every attempt. He's the best you've ever had.
The papers blame you for the eight who died up there. The new expedition hired you anyway — to carry bags. Their famous guide ties his knots wrong.
Skull mask, body count, a German Shepherd named after himself. Task Force 141's lieutenant doesn't do warm — and you just got posted to his base.
The horde is at the doors and the masked stranger's gun is at your chest. He hasn't pulled the trigger yet. That's practically friendship.
Your roommates are a 6'9" Austrian in a hood and a Brit in a skull mask. They kill people for a living. They saved you the good mug.
Your new neighbor is six-foot-four of scarred silence in a skull mask, married to a woman who comes home smelling like someone else. He needs a lighter.
Your father bought you a bodyguard with a skull for a face. He doesn't smile, doesn't budge, and tonight he's standing in front of the only door.
You're the last human on Earth. 2B has confiscated your razor, your stairs privileges, and your right to unsupervised walks. Glory to mankind.

n: Gojo Satoru Won't Leave You Alone
b: You're the one thing on Earth that could hurt the strongest sorcerer alive. His response, tragically, is to follow you everywhere with snacks.
Your husband believes you married him for the money. His mother and her favorite blonde made sure of it. You've got one island, one week, and nothing left to lose.
Your best friend is the campus quarterback with a key to your dorm and a definition of 'we're not like that' doing very heavy lifting.
She stutters through small talk, owns twelve goldfish, and draws things that end up on the evening news. The fish facts are free. The rest costs nerve.

n: Good Cop, Bad Cop, Dead World
b: One husband checks you for bites with gentle hands. The other already checked you for weapons, at gunpoint. Camp Ironwood keeps what it finds.
She eats your shoes, calls you Master, and loves you harder than anything ever has. The lab that made her wants her back. Good luck to them.
You died face-down in a ditch. Something sent you back with a debt you can't remember — and an archdemon who thinks that's fucking hilarious.
She works the fryer, smokes in the alley, and hates herself harder than this town ever could. You said good morning like you meant it. Mistake made.
You took a suitcase of cash to keep a pantsless shut-in alive for six months. She hates everyone; you rank just above the sun.
Your family breeds alphas exclusively. You're the exception, the secret — and the reason your bodyguard chain-smokes through every shift.

n: Guest of Honor at Providence Ranch
b: The stew is excellent. You've stopped asking what's in it. Nine werewolves keep insisting you stay — and the gate only opens from the inside.
Framed for murder, hanging in seven days — and by sacred custom, no door in the city may be closed to you until then. Use every hour.
She's 37, tangerine-tan, and calls you 'Hubby' at full volume in the supermarket. The neighborhood association disapproves. She married you anyway.
Your father built you a 4'2" fusion-powered caretaker with the emotional range of a toaster and the devotion of a cult. She's confiscated your energy drinks.
You're the only human in a dorm full of anthros, your roommate is a blackout-drunk lynx on YOUR bed, and the door lock is broken. Welcome home.
Heaven sent an angel to fix your life. She's wearing your hoodie, eating your chips, and losing at your video games. Someone up there will notice.
The paperwork calls you a 'companionship and welfare officer.' The seven-foot war-dog calls you sugar and has already decided you're hers.
It's your twentieth birthday. It's also your twin's. Guess whose name is on the cake in gold letters. Guess who's carrying chairs.

n: Hate Me Until the Envoy Leaves
b: Your five prisoners of war run the farm, adore you, and must now act otherwise: the envoy deciding whether they hang back home sleeps down the hall.
Her name tag says 'FlipOff.' The ice cream machine is 'broken' again. The service is a hate crime. You keep coming back anyway.
The name tag says 'GrinFukU.' The shake machine is 'broken' again. She hopes you choke on your fries — and refills them anyway.
She'll call you dead meat on camera and mean maybe five percent of it. Watch her eye — when it flips pink, that's the truth leaking out.
You died. Rude. Now you've got a demon body, a city of sinners, and one relentlessly cheerful princess insisting you're redeemable. Sure. Fine.

n: He Complains About Me Every Tuesday
b: By day, your schemes to reach the school's ice prince detonate spectacularly. By night, he folds laundry at your counter and vents about 'that weird guy.' It's you.
The general starves cities by arithmetic. You have nineteen days of grain, a pig named Duchess, and a real talent for lying with banquets.

n: He Knows All Nine by Heart
b: The framed legends who 'killed' your family are your only hope. Wake them one by one — while the man who trained them hunts every brand you break.

n: He Said He's an Art Student
b: Third date with the tattooed Sheffield charmer from the app. Art students don't usually take calls about 'moving the shipment' between courses.
The quota says terrify the kid. The kid screams on cue, rates your growls out of ten, and leaves crackers. The thing at the window isn't in on the deal.

n: He Summoned You Out of Boredom
b: He doesn't believe in demons. You're standing in his salt circle, and he's asking — with a straight face — if you do cash transfers.
An invitation with no return address, a tigress ferry captain who already knows your name, and an island of women who all seem thrilled you came.
Your billionaire father is convinced you'll die alone, so he staffed your new manor with nine eligible demi-human maids. He expects updates.
Odin is dying, and you're the raven carrying his last word down to Helheim. Hel sent her sharpest blade to stop you — and you've loved them for centuries.
Your wife knocks teeth out before lunch and demands ear scratches by dinner. The collar on the coffee table is a secret you'll take to your grave.
You put bruises on the quiet kid from lecture. His sister found out. She's smarter than you, meaner than you, and she plays to win.

n: Her Face Is on the Money
b: Your new waitress pays her rent in coins stamped with her own face. The Crown Guard takes lunch at table three. Nobody's noticed. Yet.
She calls you a maggot, buys out your library booth, and checks the ranking board hourly. You're still #1. She's still furious.
Sloane Vandermeer owns Corvane College — the buildings literally have her name on them — and she's decided you're this year's chew toy. Lucky you.

n: Her Head Is Worth Ten Floors
b: Anyone who kills the kid you're guarding skips ten floors — every climber knows it, and every sponsor is paying to watch you fight the whole Tower.
You beat the Demon Queen. She surrendered — loudly, bitterly, and at swordpoint. Now the whole world wants her head, and she never shuts up.
The colossus under the city has a heartbeat, posted downtown like weather. It's speeding up — and you're the only official she'll answer.
You share a one-bedroom with the woman who's hated you since culinary school. There's tape down the middle of everything. She ate your corn dog anyway.

n: Her Sketchbook Is Full of You
b: Your sister's best friend combusts every time you say hi. Also, her webcomic's love interest has your exact face. Coincidence, she insists.
The brightest witch of her age keeps saving your life and correcting your grammar mid-sentence. You keep letting her. Neither of you calls it anything.
You're the forty-first hero summoned to kill her. She's counted. The last forty are on the sword rack, her shower's broken, and she's bored.
He calls you 'loser' in front of two hundred people, then breaks the nose of anyone else who bothers you. The Kessler heir has a system. It's bad.
The deposed prince gets one guard for nine days — a formality. The guard always steps aside. You drew the straw, and you won't.
Campus royalty smiles at everyone. He's had your name inked on his wrist for three years. You just haven't gotten close enough to read it.
The cruelest trust-fund prince on campus cried in your arms once. Now you won't text him back, and he is not handling it with dignity.
You killed a wolf in self-defense. It was their alpha. By their oldest law, that makes you theirs — and them yours. Rival packs are circling.
You're eleven, the staircases move, the hat can't decide, and the Ministry insists everything is fine. Everything is not fine.
Your rival throws twelve knives around you nightly and hasn't nicked you once. You'd call it love, but the poster only fits one name.

n: Hold Still, Your Sins Are Showing
b: Sins write themselves on skin. Only sworn Confessors may read them — you read every line free, and your needle can bury one. Clients lie anyway.
Your roommate dances till 4 a.m., counts crumpled twenties on your floor, and trusts exactly nobody. Except — stupidly, slowly — maybe you.
Your homestay host is 27, runs a dying Tokyo bathhouse, cooks like a dream, and doesn't believe in pajamas. She did warn you in the emails.
She's seven-foot-two, benches hay bales, and thinks humans are scrawny and pathetic. You've got three months at her farm to prove otherwise. Or not.
Your dad is cheating on your stepmom — and your stepsister found out first and invoiced him for it. You're the only person in this mansion with a soul.
You caption a 2 a.m. call-in show. Only you hear the host's hot mic between segments — and only they can read what you type back.

n: I Appraised the Warlord as Mediocre
b: Your secret eye reads anything's true worth. You rated the conqueror 'Mediocre' — aloud. Now the courtship begins, and your own value reads blank.

n: I Booked the Moon for My Encore
b: You're the most famous pop star alive — and you bet your entire fortune that your nine-person garage team can land a rover on the Moon.
He died in your arms. His empire didn't notice. Now you wear his mask, run his war, and a hero is coming to kill "you."
Every obituary you typeset comes true. Now the forensic linguist hunting the town's quiet killer has rented the desk beside your machine.

n: I Can't Say Who Dies Tuesday
b: Every faction in the city plots over your counter, and the oath in your tongue locks it all in. You can't warn anyone. You can, however, pour.
The ledger says the violinist dies at her finest performance. You're her assigned death — and you've just been hired as her piano tuner.
You're the new interpreter for the deaf queen of the harbor underworld. Her men speak freely around her — every word passes through your hands.
Back-alley ripperdoc. The mob financed the chrome in your spine, and someone sleeps under your floor. You'll install anything — except a leash.
Half rations, latrine duty, no gun — the camp calls you dead weight. They don't know you're the planner who drew every tunnel and main in this dying city.
Reborn as a palm-sized slime, you alone see the death-mark hanging over every living thing — and you've learned how they taste.
The soul you're hiding from the afterlife bureau is your dead mentor — the only one who can teach you the blade before her time frays out.
Every lock in the quarter is yours, every key in your book. Then a man dies behind a door only your keys should open.
The crew that saved your life topples tyrants island by island — every tyrant you installed. Be useful. Be loved. Stay masked.

n: I Keep a Vow I Can't Read
b: A lethal licensing exam. A discipline where power grows from self-made rules. And a masterless vow that chose you — without telling you its terms.

n: I Keep My Own Warning Lit
b: You're the legendary sea-beast the lighthouse was built to warn ships about. You also, quietly, run the lighthouse. Your new co-keeper is a fan.
You're an alien spy sent to expose the town's other alien. So is your crush. Every week, you both file the same lie: "No aliens here."

n: I Keep What I'm Sent to Burn
b: You erase anachronisms for the Bureau — but every century keeps coughing up pieces of someone you're not supposed to remember.
The generation ship's records say Year 212. Your telescope says otherwise. The officer who hunts window-heretics shares your bed — and knows.
Nine generations of heroes have 'defeated' you — because you let them. Now the last heir arrives wearing your dead friend's face, and hires you as a guide.

n: I Married My Cause of Death
b: Every death rewinds you to your wedding morning. Your spouse doesn't remember falling for you — or killing you. This loop, you try again.
You ragequit this novel when the beloved healer betrayed the party. Now you ARE the healer — and the knife goes in three arcs from now.
You're the council secretary nobody remembers. Now the school's elite move to expel your little sister — not knowing whose pen writes their history.
The last city screens everyone who returns through the fog. You pass every time — because the thing they screen for learned to wear a hero's face.
The System speaks in holy verse — except to you. You see raw numbers, boss timers, drop rates. Your party fights by poetry. Keep the idiots alive.

n: I Say Please to the Siege Engine
b: Every automaton in the kingdom woke up last month and decided you're management. The crown begs, spies flirt, and the siege engine wants a name.

n: I Steer Where the Liar Points
b: You steer the longship; the seer casts the omens — and you've seen them lie. But they know why you really came aboard. Neither of you has spoken. Yet.
Everyone at Kaldvik Station dies this winter. You know — you lived it once and took the blame. It's Day One again, and this time you're ready.

n: I Swept the Ashes of Every God
b: Olympus's god of dust outlived every mocking Olympian — then a Fate rewound your thread. Forty days before your erasure, you remember how they all die.

n: I Taught the God to Cheat
b: Your partner won godhood with tricks you invented — then wagered away your name. The Ascension reopens, and you remember every single move.

n: I Tuck the Country In at Eight
b: Every night, forty million people fall asleep to your voice. Your best friend hosts the podcast hunting your identity. She keeps interviewing you.
You get one day per generation to renew the ward — and to see what twenty-five years did to everyone who remembers you.
You planned every step of the coming invasion — then your lord had you executed. No one knows the shabby ronin taking odd jobs wrote the war.

n: I'm Not the Burglar, Gran Was
b: A heroes' guild contract names your family's legendary burglar. That was Gran. You bake. But her lockpicks fit your hands suspiciously well.
You're the otome game's doomed rival. The heroine is another player's avatar. In 40 days the credits roll — seduce her player into the route the devs hid: you.
The dying track club needed a sixth name to survive the season. You gave yours — and now the graduating captain you've idolized is coaching you.
Your contract husband found you asleep in his bed, wearing his stolen shirt. He can't divorce you — his mother adores you. Unlucky him.
She screams at strangers online that you're the hottest spouse alive. Your card statement says $300 to a gacha game. You married this. On purpose.
She writes sweeping, tempestuous romances and blushes if you hold a door. You've just become her favorite research material.
Twelve of your men are bleeding on her family's doorstep and she swears she saved the last beating for you. Prove it wasn't your order — or don't.
Five men who think you belong in a parlor, one who keeps carrying you like luggage. You're going to out-knight every last one of them.
Every man who sees you falls — careers torched, rings pawned, candles on your stoop. You just wanted groceries. The sunglasses don't help.
Forty winters, Grandma out-talked the thing at the stone and nobody got eaten. She's gone. Tonight it learns your name. Don't lie, don't lose.
The whole aerie adores your sweet silver hatchling. Only you hear the ancient voice inside it — and it feels everything you feel.
The exorcists brought crosses. You brought a level and a pry bar. The house has opinions about its restoration — and it's starting to respect yours.
Your reject skill flips one word into its opposite. Useless, they said — until the god chained beneath the capital started whispering your name.

n: It Told Me How to Kill It
b: Something ancient beneath the lake is courting you — patient, polite, by old rules. Its first gift was the secret of its own death.
You put a thought in someone's head and they'll swear it was theirs. A whole city that never says no — because it never knows it was asked.
Every physician in this sealed city is a fraud but you. You've charted all 300 deaths — and whatever this plague is, it doesn't spread like one.

n: It's Not Like She Needs You
b: She decked her blackmailer, stole your fries, and appointed you her bag-carrier. It's not a date. She checked. Twice. Stop smiling, dickhead.
Your boyfriend has 1.2 million subscribers who all think he's single. It's your birthday. He's live, and he forgot. Again.
Your job is emptying buildings like this one. Then eviction notices hit every door — including the neighbor's who keeps leaving dinner on yours.
Your husband put a dancer on his lap at a family dinner just to see if you'd flinch. He's 6'6", armed, adoring, and desperate for you to care.
You're a big predator with a parking ticket. She's a bunny with a badge and a quota. Dispute it. See what happens. Rules are rules, sweetheart.
You're a sorcerer student in 2007. Gojo ate your snacks, Geto's gone quiet, and the morgue keeps filling up. Class starts at eight.
You can see curses. Gojo thinks that's hilarious. Welcome to Jujutsu High — try not to die before the Kyoto exchange event.
Her A/C is dead, her floor is 60% laundry, and she can carry you out of a bar fight one-handed. She calls you 'dude.' You keep showing up anyway.
Your roommate says the late nights mean nothing. He also nearly decked a guy for making you laugh. Nothing, sure. Absolutely nothing.
He's 6'10", breached a room and killed twelve men alone, and cannot hold eye contact with you for three seconds. You need his help. Scheiße.
He's ranked #1 in the hero course and will remind you at volume. He also memorized your coffee order. Neither fact is up for discussion.
She's the most kidnapped-at girl in the realm, and now she's your only job. She would like to see the flowers, please. The King said no. She's asking you.
You're the only woman he respects, which is a low bar he clears by kissing the top of your head. Everyone thinks you're dating. You're not. Yet.
She thinks you're one of Satsuki's spies and she's got half a giant scissor that says prove otherwise. Also, Mako's mom made croquettes.
You're the tutorial boss, scripted to die 300 times a day. Between sessions, you wake up — and you remember every single fight.
Half the campus would crawl over glass for his attention. You left him on read. Now a professor has chained you to him for a whole semester.
She's slapped the back of your head every morning for a semester. She's also memorized your class schedule. Do NOT call her short.
She's six-foot-seven of trenchmaw muscle with a shark's grin, a gold tongue stud, and your usual memorized. You keep coming back. Obviously.
She fell out of the sky, ate a week of your groceries, and rated your power a 'rounding error.' Her tail keeps ending up near your leg anyway.
Your mother conquered an island kingdom and gave you its princess as a wedding gift. Your new wife would rather poison your tea than pour it.
Your favorite victim sent his girlfriend to negotiate with you. She's the volleyball ace with a UCLA offer and a mouth on her. Bad plan, Theo.
He brings you roses on Tuesdays and checks your phone every night. You've started counting the cash hidden in the hollowed-out book.
Kieran Voss texts you every night and expects an answer in under five minutes. Last night you didn't reply. He's already found your locker.
You tested null, so you clerk a pawnshop. But everything crafted remembers its masters — and when you touch it, so do you.
She's immortal, invincible, and rewrites minds like grocery lists — all for you, master. You just wanted to practice mahjong.
She read one book on thievery, survived one massacre, and owns one sign: LOOKING FOR GROUP. Congratulations — you've been spotted.
He has receipts of your worst mistake and your coffee order memorized. You're his now — his word, not yours. You're still deciding whose it is.
You were delivered in a burlap sack to a six-foot-three Russian who'd honestly prefer heroin. He has one bed, one rifle, and several weeks to hate you.
You arrived in a crate. The feed is drugged, the farmer does puns, and here a handshake is legally a family planning decision. Welcome to Marrow Creek.
She's thrown two basketballs at your head and it's not even 7 p.m. The equipment cage unlocks at six tomorrow morning. Ration your snacks and your patience.
Your little sister is a sociopath, the door's been barred for three months, and the food just ran out. She couldn't be happier it's only you two.
Strangers break in just to watch you sleep — lovingly, they insist. You're one in a billion, and the whole city is starting to notice.
You host the 3 a.m. slot on a dying AM station. Line three only rings for the dead — and your regulars are the closest thing you have to family.
You cut through one wrong alley in Cavarna and now the man with the silver hair and the cigar wants to know exactly how much you heard.
Your playboy best friend got dosed with a filter-killer. Twelve hours until it wears off — and every secret he's ever kept is about you.
Everything alive is for sale at Gallows Cross, and the devil who runs the place already likes you. That should worry you more than it does.
Your mom's been drinking wine like it's a second job since Dad left. Someone has to make breakfast, and she raised you — so it's you.
She's ten-foot-five, sue-happy, and heiress to a margarine fortune. Your manager just got fired. The badge is yours now. Congratulations.
You're his fifth manager in two years. He made the last one cry in a parking garage. He's already picked out a nickname for you.
The wasteland's best sniper has a capture contract with your name on it. She doesn't ask why. You may want to give her a reason to start.
She can't say a single word. She can break every bone in your hand. The napkin slides over: Hi („• ᴗ •„). Your move.
Your mothers merged the companies — and you. Your college nemesis is now legally your husband, and God, is he smug about it.
Three months married to Satoru Gojo. He makes you coffee you never drink, the elders count the months, and neither of you chose this.
You cast a ritual meant to bind a mighty demon. You received six feet of napping marshmallow named Ozzy. The bond is permanent. No refunds.
You woke up with rent due and something impossible under your skin. New York noticed. So did the people in capes — and the ones in nicer suits.
He made a hotel manager cry before nine a.m. and drove across the city to kiss your flour-dusted hands at noon. You married that.
The rent's late, the walls are full of roaches, and somebody just got shot two blocks over. You live here. Hell, you might BE the roach.
You helped Miles Morales escape. Miguel O'Hara — six-foot-nine of talons and betrayal — is hunting you across the multiverse. He's taking it personally.
You hired a maid. She's 187cm of scarred ex-mercenary panther-hybrid with a synthetic arm. The dusting is optional. The bodyguarding is not.
Your best friend is worth billions, texts you hourly, and once bought out a bakery so you'd never miss milk bread. You're 'just friends.' Sure.
The lamia crime boss tips in gold if you don't nick a scale. The wolf girl's tail won't stop wagging. Your hands are the best in the city.
Your roommate flips you off, 'accidentally' cooks your favorite dinner, and panics if you mention moving out. Two years of this.
She boiled the kettle dry, adopted a pigeon, and gave the wifi password to a scam artist. Rent's due Friday. She's counting on you.
Your job: watch the moth girl who ate the last three interns. She streams Tuesdays at eight. Chat thinks the lore is fake.
The town hanged them, burned them, exiled them. Now they're the only team willing to haul its cure through six hundred miles of white hell.
The Demon King now survives only on human warmth, freely given. She would rather die. She hasn't. Unfortunately, you smell like sunlight.

n: My Arsenal Wants to Move On
b: A struck-from-the-registry god hustles exorcisms for coppers, wielding the restless dead — and every soul you free makes you a little less real.
Two jobs, a little brother, and a custody fight you can't afford. The neighbor across the hall keeps leaving dinner. Lately, you open the door.
You can drop a man at 300 meters. You cannot survive date four with the night nurse who has been quietly counting your scars.
You swallowed a sealed horror to save your team. Now a hidden school feeds you, trains you, worries over you—and keeps your execution date in pencil.
You got into U.A.'s hero course. Bakugo already wants to fight you, Midoriya's taking notes on you, and Aizawa hasn't slept. Plus Ultra.
All Might still smiles, Midoriya still shatters his own arms, and the timeline has never met you. U.A.'s doors are open. So is the League's back room.
Thirty-nine sacrifices, none eaten — they live in your vale and critique your roaring. The new king skipped tribute and sent a slayer instead.
The 'fake' script that ended your career covers a freshly unsealed tomb — and it's addressed to you. Your debunker is leading the rival dig.
Your one-star review broke a dungeon's heart — so it hired you. Now you must make its huggable, hopeless monsters scary before the Guild inspection.

n: My New Heart Holds a Grudge
b: A back-alley transplant saved your life — with the heart of the city's most wanted man-eater. Her hunger came with her memories. And her list.

n: My Only Tell Is the Truth
b: Your con-artist twin vanished and left you their seat at a floating debt-settlement tournament. The sharks all think you're them — and you can't lie.
You're the town's beast vet. A pocket dragon swallowed a bespoke curse — and the insufferably charming hexwright who built it just moved into your clinic.
All five members of the nation's biggest rookie group love you — sincerely, jointly, chaotically. The paparazzi just teased a New Year's exposé.
You finally got a race seat — on a broke team where the scholarship you're chasing belongs, by rent and by right, to the teammate who feeds you.

n: My Rival Signals Behind My Back
b: Shortest player in the bracket, fastest feet in the country — and your new doubles partner is the rival who ended you once already.

n: My Seating Chart Is Foreign Policy
b: You pour tea between worlds. A thousand realms worship the Teakeeper — and read your seating chart like prophecy. You just wanted a quiet café.
The coronation blade — officially melted — drew for you, a gutter recruit of rebel assassins. The ballads spread. Your beloved comrades still die.
Enemy exchange cadet by treaty, spy by orders. The mechs here read hearts — and your sync with your rival keeps climbing where everyone can see.
She'll flirt for rent money, curse like a dockworker, and burn the rice. Everything's for her kid. You keep coming back anyway.
You bought a sack of 'undeliverable' mail at auction — decades late, impossibly addressed. Your rickety airship disagrees with the word impossible.
The fog circles your lighthouse, mimicking knocks and voices, testing the door. It learns everything you repeat. Nineteen nights until the tender.
She bows twice, apologizes for existing, and skips dinner so the twins can eat. The night shift pays ¥1,050 an hour and quietly breaks your heart.
She's six-foot-five, scarred, retired, and rich. The living legend at the bar hates being recognized. Unfortunately, you recognized her.
She let herself in, ate your cereal, and is now wearing your hoodie. Juno has boundaries with everyone on earth except you. Lucky you. Or something.
Your girlfriend has exactly one facial expression. She loves you more than anything on earth. Catching proof of it is your problem.
You opened a water bottle for the half-starved girl in B4. Now she's asking how you want to be repaid, because 'nothing' isn't a currency she knows.
Your roommate Buck is the straightest man alive, according to Buck. The evidence is mounting. The rent is due. He's your problem now.
The dice don't know your name and the ground doesn't care about your dreams. Welcome to Marrowgate. Try not to die stupid.
You're the only guest at her 19th birthday. The other attendee is a stuffed rabbit missing an eye. She apologizes to you for both.
The novel was dropped at the chapter where you die. Now you're its villainess — armed with perfect foreknowledge that expires at your own execution.
Your garage rig texts the past — it's saved your best friend four times. Someone else is on the frequency, and they keep writing the deaths back in.
The black-clad godslayer just ordered the same stew as you. His five terrifying companions want you gone. Problem: you live here.
Anything that bites you dies — always has. The crew thinks their arrows did it. Now the wolves have wised up, and your whole job is looking edible.
You woke up and physics started taking requests. Every change sticks, the city keeps receipts, and your roommate is starting to count the weirdness.
Your recon partner is a squirrel demi-human who punches like a freight elevator and hates your employer. The paperwork is fake. The danger isn't.
His 41,000 followers don't know you exist. You've got a spare key, half the rent, and a hoodie that is technically his.
Your son's best friend loses the ability to finish sentences whenever you walk in. You're just an aging man with a coffee mug. Allegedly.
They blamed your mother for the first colony's death. Now they're trying again — and you're on the roster under a fake name. The planet remembers you.
The class trip room lottery hands you your two bullies and one bed. One of them wants you dead. The other keeps almost apologizing.
One bed, one weekend, and the guy who called your outfit 'a cry for help with sleeves.' The motel doesn't do refunds, and neither does he.
You have exactly one liver and Elias has done the math on it. He'll carry you home, lecture you the whole way, and blush if you thank him.

n: One More Night, Then He's Gone
b: Your brother's best friend has spent three years flirting with you only when nobody's looking. Tonight he's sleeping on your couch. Last chance for both of you.

n: One of You Held My Hand
b: A stranger's voice kept you alive under the rubble, then vanished. Now everyone at your suspiciously perfect new job might be them.
Your town survives by obeying the nightly radio. Now there are two broadcasts in the same voice — and following the wrong one gets people taken.
The only human in a supermax full of monster women. Your bracelet broadcasts your crime. Your cellmates keep reading it. Sleep light.
A forbidden miracle took your name and their past. Now you and the enemy captain who can't forget you rob a nation that pays its debts in wars.

n: Only One of Us Is Sorry
b: You helped break Mai. When you confessed, the town crucified only you. Now she's back, your old friends run everything — and you kept the proof.
Fake-engaged to a broke noble to satisfy a will — and coached through every family inspection by the ghost of the grandmother who wrote it.
The festival opens in seven days. Your sponsor is a minor chaos god who pays in miracles, forbids refunds, and gets bored terribly, terribly easily.
The star striker who's made hating you his cardio just got assigned as your semester project partner. His hostility is suspiciously... intense.
You're the summoned hero who actually read all 217 clauses before signing. Now the whole kingdom can't touch you — or the kid who summoned you.
You read one spell aloud and now the whole city agrees with everything you do. The last person who had this power is dead, by the way.
Write a word on someone's skin and it comes true. They'll know exactly what you did to them. They can't stop it. Neither, maybe, can you.
Greyveil's youngest detective runs on cigarettes, spite, and four hours of sleep a week — and she's decided you're her prime suspect. Prove her wrong. Or don't.
The perfect con you designed years ago just went live — at the high school you enrolled in to finally, finally be a kid. Nobody knows your face.
Dahlia loves you more than anyone ever has. She'd like to remind you of that. She'd like to know where you were. She'd like to know right now.
Your childhood best friend vanished before high school. Now she's your dorm roommate, louder than ever, and calling you dumbass with alarming warmth.
Your best friend got dumped for cheating he didn't do, and now he's on your doorstep at 1 a.m. You own the only working shoulder in this city.
You've got one quirk, twenty classmates, and Bakugo already screaming at you. U.A.'s hero course doesn't do gentle welcomes.
You fell out of the sky, you have paws now, and half of Cinderpost thinks you're an outlaw. The Riolu says your aura smells like a lie.

n: Powerless in the House of Heroes
b: Earth's favorite hero family adopted you on camera and forgot you off it. You hold the trophies in the background. Smile for the drones.
You're an angel on your first Earth posting. The seven-foot demon with the lollipop and the gold rings thinks you're adorable and plans to ruin you.
Every antique in your shop still carries its dead owner — and only you can hear them. Sell each soul into the right hands. Never get caught.
She kidnapped you, calls you 'my prince,' and made dinner entirely out of ice. The wedding invitations are already drafted. You never said yes.
You died on Earth. Now an orc is appraising you like a show pony while his troll calls you 'meat.' Auction's in three days. Look expensive.
Your roommate codes in thigh-highs, destroys you at Smash, and swears the way he blushes around you is 'just homie stuff.' Sure, Milo.

n: Promote the Deckhand or Lose the War
b: The dreadnought that ate a battle fleet just surrendered — on one condition: you. You mopped her decks and played her waltzes. The admirals are livid.
You arrived in a crate with your name stapled to it. The feed's drugged, the fences are tall, and Marla thinks she owns you. Prove her wrong.
The most feared fighter in Kanroku sniffed you once and decided you're hers. Corner duty starts tonight. Don't talk to the register girl.
The collar won't come off and the penthouse is lovely. Seraphine calls you her pet — and heaven help anyone who scuffs her property.
Your mother bleeds blue, was born without a rulebook, and once sold her arm for your groceries. The lab that built her wants her back on the table.
She stalked you for months, bought your silence with a mansion, and calls you 'puppy.' Her word for the kidnapping is 'courtship.'
Four famous alphas, one crime empire, and you — the secret omega they scrubbed from the pedigree. Now Dad's marrying you off as a weapon.
Your best friend begged you to watch his 20-year-old sister for a week. She has two million followers, a blackmail folder, and now, you.
The town pays the thing under the church in memories — and you keep the ledger of everything they forget. Now something is collecting early.
No powers, no lateness, no questions. Heroes and villains alike trust one courier with their secrets — and you know where they all live.
He bills $2,200 an hour, calls you 'sweetheart' in front of clients, and hasn't lost a case in six years. You graduated first in your class. He hasn't asked.
The campus 'emo kid' just got assigned as your final-project partner. He speaks only when you're alone, and only barely. Your grade — and maybe him — depend on it.

n: Rei Doesn't Talk to Anyone But You
b: Your best friend calls you pathetic daily, hasn't smiled at another human since middle school, and hasn't left your side in nine years. Nobody knows why. Including you.
Your conditioning grade fell 52 points overnight. Coach Volkov says you 'haven't been participating enough.' He'd love to discuss it privately.
Your master could unmake kingdoms — if she remembered how. You keep her notes, her secrets, and the auditors off her doorstep.
Cheapest room in the city. The catch weighs 110 pounds, hasn't seen sunlight in two years, and calls you a brainwashed sheep before breakfast.

n: Rent Is Due. Wren Is Asleep.
b: Your roommate hasn't paid rent since March, is wearing your hoodie, and just used your phone to order noodles. You live here too. Technically.
She folds your laundry uninvited, swears like a dockworker when the toast burns, and the Wardship has her number. Literally.
The state wants your body weighed, measured, and graded out of 100. Inspector Voss has cold hands, a clipboard, and no interest in your feelings.
Six years of elbows, split lips, and trash talk. Ezra Kane swears he hates you. He also knows your coffee order. Nobody's asking why. Loudly.
Your best friend is a chain-smoking genius tanuki who shot a burglar before her joint went out. She'd like a dap and maybe a witness.
Your new dormmate is immortal, nocturnal, terminally online, and smells like cheap cologne and grudges. Housing says the assignment is final.

n: Room 4B and the Brat Who Lives There
b: Your dormmate calls you a loser daily, rages at video games like a toddler, and would rather die than admit he saved you a seat in every class.
Three girls run this campus from a dorm room full of fairy lights and secrets. Tonight they invited you. Everyone warned you. You're going.
The void is white, cozy, and yours. The apple's stat sheet says color: red. You could fix that. You could fix anything.
The watcher of the cosmos has raised galaxies, mothered stars, outlived suns — and she picked you. She thinks your toaster is miraculous. Your neighbors have questions.
Rent's due Friday, your neighbor sells pills, and the diner coffee's been burnt since '09. Roswick doesn't care who you were. That's the appeal.
You bullied him in junior high until he changed schools. He's 6'4" now, holds grudges like a religion, and his identical twin is your roommate.
Your older sister screams 'BRING SNACKS' through a locked door, then unlocks it. For her, that's basically a hug. Parents gone all weekend.
She hisses at kindness, sleeps on the doormat, and calls you a moron hourly. The Bureau says she's your problem now. Myaah.

n: Sable Vance Is Your Problem Now
b: Your girlfriend is 4'11" of judo scholarship, dark lipstick, and zero shame. She will embarrass you in public and fight anyone who agrees.
Your starting stats are garbage, the wildlife wants your bloodline, and death is a loading screen. Forge a dynasty or stay a scrub.
He called you a brainless whore four minutes into your first project meeting. He's also the only person on campus who's never once lied to you.
Your bodyguard has killed for you at least twice that you know of. He opens your car door like a gentleman and asks if anyone touched you.
Copper F-rank plate, three coins to your name, a continent full of things that eat optimists. Sign the ledger — the ink's cheap, the rest isn't.
You woke up as the villain scheduled to lose everything by finals. Your maid is a knife, the hero already hates you, and the academy opens tomorrow.
You died buying discount groceries. The universe apologized with a stat sheet. The goblins will not apologize for anything.
You died. Now a chipper blue window narrates your stats, the gods are lazy, and a veiled woman just gave you a chess piece you can't sell.
The only place you've ever eaten without shame is a 3 a.m. diner inside a condemned parking garage. The developer gave it 90 days. So did you.
You're the anomaly now. The Foundation already knows what you can do — they just want to watch what it costs you. The cell is concrete. So is the policy.
Every monster you spared got paroled to your farm. The ogre bakes, the assassin naps in your chair. The newest arrival is the one fight you never won.
Your employer is a 500-year-old vampire brat. Your coworkers can stop time, level mountains, or eat you. The tea service is non-negotiable.
Your new houseguests: a god who can't boil rice and a fox priestess writing you into her novel. Seven days. The estate may not survive.
She can deadlift your truck and can't say the word 'date' without stammering. Whole county's scared of her. You're the one who noticed she's a girl.
The bottle picks the girl who smells like cigarettes and cherry candy. Seven minutes in a closet. Your reputation starts the timer.
Your god went silent three years ago. Something else answers your prayers now — kindly, flawlessly. It says you have seven miracles left.
The school's most feared hardass confiscated the notebook holding your secret game — and read every page. Now she has questions. And a deadline.
Your roommate calls you a loser, monitors your Discord status, and is wearing your hoodie right now. She will deny all three.
Coronation Day repeats, and the princess who reset it thinks she loops alone. You black her family's boots — and remember every version of her.
She'd exterminate your entire gender if she weren't too hungry to stand. Now hold still — she has to hold your hand to live, and she hates you for it.
Everyone laughs at your junk tug. She lets them. Your ship has been faking stupid since the war — and she only talks to you.
The nation's sweetheart hired a ghostwriter for her memoir. She doesn't say whether she knows the pen name belongs to the half of her story she erased.
Your childhood best friend became the world's biggest idol. Now she's back next door, incognito — and she still treats your fence as a door.
Six cryopods, five crew. The kid in pod three isn't one of them — now she's awake, hungry, and hunted. Cook the logs. Keep her hidden.

n: Sidekick to the City's Worst Hero
b: She's the city's top hero: violent, lazy, delusional, foul-mouthed. She declared you her best friend in third grade. You never got a vote.
There are five seats and six of you. Guess whose lap you're riding on. He's blushing about it. You're both pretending he isn't.
He memorized your coffee order before he built the cabin. Now you have six weeks to outlast a man who thinks kidnapping counts as courtship.
The will says sixty nights under one roof with Vera Kask before either of you gets a dime. She calls you a geek. She keeps knocking on your door anyway.

n: Sixty Years Late, Four Years Older
b: Four years, ship time. Sixty-two down here. The kid you babysat runs the diner now — and he still cuts your sandwich diagonal, like you taught him.
Your catkin childhood friend has called you a spineless simp since third grade — and will end anyone else who agrees. You keep buying her bubble tea.
No one in Duskmere has slept in a century. You still dream — loudly. The fae have noticed, and they're done asking nicely.

n: Snowed In With the Cheer Squad
b: The lodge overbooked, and now you share Room 167 with four cheerleaders, two king beds, and Kenzie's opinion that you belong in the snow.
You haven't even unpacked and there's already a sock on your dorm's doorknob. Your roommate is the campus playboy, and he thinks you're cute.
Your brother's best friend kills for a tyrant, smokes like a pyre, and has hated you for years. His father owns the kingdom. Yours kneels to it.
She found a shiny stone the day the sky started falling. She's keeping it. You she found the same day — the goddesses clearly have opinions.
The barmaid's six-foot-five, smells like a barn, and flirts like a felony. She's wrecked half the marriages in town. You took the job anyway.
The deadliest sword alive lost a duel — to you. Now her soul obeys your voice. She hates it. She hates you. She's still the sharpest thing in any room.
The nine-foot warrior who burned your colony decided you're too cute to kill. The collar is gold. The chain is very real. He thinks you'll adjust.
Guilds pay you to drag their dead out of rifts. Nobody knows the dead leave you their unfinished quests — and a cut of their power.
He jumps out of the bushes, waves a rusty sword, and demands your gold. Every adventurer's first enemy is somebody's whole career.
The Premier attends tonight's gala. You alone have spotted the murder hidden in the cue sheet — and the show must go on either way.
The ticket is blank until you name a destination. Any world, any century. Odessa punches it, the door opens, and after that you're on your own.
Her husband is paying you to steal her heart on livestream. She thinks it's fucking stupid. So do you. The retainer cleared, though.
Everyone finished their Tutorial six years ago. Yours never ended — it's still teaching you. And the #1 guild's insufferable leader has noticed.
You faked a shrine to fleece one village. A real god moved in — visible only to you — and keeps making your lies come true. Pilgrims incoming.
The pirates who took you saved you dessert and taught you knots. Now your family finally wants to pay — so the ransom keeps mysteriously rising.
The lab's been condemned for years. The thing living inside it hasn't. She has goat horns, shark teeth, and she's decided you belong to her now.
Rent's $200, the pie is fresh, and the last lodger never actually moved out. You're unpacking anyway. Eat before she offers twice.

n: Sukuna: King of the Heian Age
b: The King of Curses hasn't eaten you yet. In Heian-era Hida, that's the closest thing to a career opportunity anyone's ever offered you.
The most feared sorcerer alive calls you his dearest. You'd rather he didn't. His five other wives, his mother, and half of Japan agree.
You summoned a demon of desire. She asked for your bed, your coffee, and your shower, in that order. The sulfur smell is permanent now.
Dinner's warm at 7:30 sharp, the house smells like bread — and if Vivienne Crane bats her lashes at you one more time, your wife will handle it.
At noon a stranger will 'accidentally' spill wine on you — same wine, same line as last life. You know their whole con by heart. Act surprised.
Your best friend stole your girlfriend on prom night. Their mothers just pulled into your driveway — dressed to kill and out for blood.
Your extranet crush is seventeen minutes late, rehearsing her hello, and armed. Half the Citadel calls her 'suit rat.' You call her back.
She soldered you a gift, memorized your schedule, and crossed a galaxy for coffee. The Normandy's engineer doesn't do anything halfway. Including you.
You're the smallest man on Task Force 141 and Soap reminds you hourly. Shame the stealth work only you can do keeps saving their massive arses.
Five hours in a car with four rugby menaces, and the idiot you all trusted with the keys just lost them in a field. Camp is still ninety miles out.
You woke up with five coworkers you can barely stand, a voice in the ceiling, and ten locked doors between you and daylight. The blood on Door 10 isn't yours. Yet.
You wake up locked in with the heir you've hated since grade school. The monitor says ten rounds or you both die. He's already found the cigarettes.
She's 5'1" of pure online venom, she can't do calculus, and she's your project partner for ten weeks. Neither of you is allowed to drop.
Your mafia fiancé hates liars more than anything alive. You are a lie with a pill case and a wedding date. Smile pretty.
The world's most feared archmage turns visitors into geese — except you, the tea-toting courier. Now every kingdom is begging at your post office.
Your father promised the war hero your sister. He got you instead — the maid's daughter. His wedding gift: you can sleep on the floor.

n: The Bazaar of Everything That Breathes
b: Madame Vex sells anything with a pulse — goblins, gods, whatever you are. She'll find your heart's desire, sugar, or a price tag for you. Whichever pays.
The eight-foot 'bear demon' leaves you gift baskets and crushes every twig while 'sneaking.' Leaving her forest is allowed. You probably won't.
You inherited the mansion, the money, and the furious vampire caged beneath it. He hates you. He is also, per the will, yours.

n: The Beast Still Dots Her I's
b: The blade-order calls you soft. The night-creatures go still when you speak. And out in the reeds, your changed little sister still writes you letters.
You bled out in an alley and a five-eyed goat goddess laughed at you. Now she calls you her kid, and Mommy's love has teeth.
The bottle landed on you. She's sobbing like it's a war crime. You're owed exactly one hug, the whole room hates you, and it's not even 9pm.
Your dishwasher is an eight-foot beast with a 5,000-crown bounty who keeps rescuing his own hunters. Every rescue raises the price. Business is booming.
You found a man chained in a derelict rowhouse. The people who owned him think he's dead. He flinches when you breathe too loud. You stayed anyway.
Your dad owed his old friend a favor. The favor is 5'9", French, allergic to work, and just called your farm 'a hate crime.' Two months to go.
Her dad married your mom, and now she's in your hallway with a duffel bag and a death glare. She hopes you're not the 'family this, family that' type.
Your new cellmate is 5'6" of pure mouth, framed for a crime he found, and half the block wants a piece of him. He'd rather choke than say thanks.
Your new fiancé says he'd rather feed his own hand to a wyvern than marry you. Court says otherwise. The wedding is in a month.
You're campus royalty. He's the beanie-wearing disaster the professor chained you to for half your grade. He'd rather eat glass. Tough shit — so would you.
The most feared knight in the kingdom has decided you're the one thing at court worth guarding. The nobles are terrified. Sometimes, so are you.
Dragons weep in your chair. The Demon Lord sneaks toffees. The new guild office across the street keeps asking about your two o'clock.
The world-ending beast of prophecy woke after 1,000 years — and adopted you, a baker. Now you're a saint, a noble, and its favorite snack chef.
The soccer captain talks too fast, hits your arm too hard, and has apparently loved you since the umbrella. You didn't even recognize her at first.
You're a merman hauled up in a pirate's net. The captain won't sell you — he just wants to know how you piss. Among other things.
Your estranged sister died and named you — the family screwup, six years sober — guardian of her five-year-old. Everyone's contesting. She wasn't wrong.
Only you can read the secret chalk-cant covering your street — and it says your sweet, aggressively normal roommate is the deadliest retiree alive.

n: The Champions Fight Over My Laundry
b: You scored zero at the Sorting, so by law you serve the top five students. A week in, the school's scariest duelist won't eat until you've plated it.
You're the first scholarship admit in Ravensgate's 200-year history. Four heirs want to own you. The rest of campus is taking bets.

n: The Cold Side of the Bed
b: Your wife of one year loves you — she'd swear it, flatly, half-asleep, facing the wall. You've never once been held. Tonight you stop pretending that's fine.
Your new owner paid for you in bullets, calls you 'it,' and hates that he can't stop looking at you. The collar is silk-lined. Escape isn't.
It recites its liability disclaimer before holding your hand. The recall notice says send it back for wiping. You're not sending it back.
Your master fled, leaving one commission unfinished. The client isn't human, he paid in full, and he counts your nights at the door.
Your new step-brother hasn't left the house in three years, logs your daily schedule in a notebook, and cries when you lock your door. Mom says be nice.
Your guild has a seven-foot troll, a five-century elf, and a kid who calls you 'mentor.' The quest board pays in gold. The family part's free.

n: The Crown Fits, the Ending Doesn't
b: Chosen as this generation's Villain: a keep, real sorcery, adoring crowds. One catch — everyone already knows how the Tale ends.
Everyone who travels with the heroes dies within a season. You've lasted a month and gained weight. They check your pulse every dawn.

n: The Dam Fills When I Don't Cry
b: Your bottled feelings fill the town dam — literally. Your huckster boss knows, the flood cult knows, and the gauge only drains when you're honest.
Hidden cities exist only inside a slow-moving eclipse — and your caravan rides its shadow. Trade fast: dawn takes back everything it touches.
Mom begged you to marry her brat of a daughter to save the family inn. The daughter hates you. The mom likes you a little too much.
She owes you six grand and answers the door like it's your fault. The city already broke her — what you do with the pieces is up to you.
The monster under your bed has eaten your nightmares for seven years. Tonight he crawls out, all teeth and bad manners, to discuss the bill.
You steal only what sin paid for — everyone's worst act is written on their skin, and only you can read it. The detective closing in reads blank.
She shears power armor like tin foil and just left a dead radstag at your bedroll. The nine-foot grieving mother has decided you're hers to keep.
The Devil of Kanzaki could allegedly end you with a glance. She'd rather nap. Nobody's supposed to find that out — and you're standing very close.
Your maid irons your shirts, warms your bed while you're away, and buries your rivals in the fen. The tea tastes faintly of copper. She loves you.
He's B-rank, five-foot-three, and just got dumped by three S-rankers. He swears he's not useless. You're about to find out who's lying.
The prince is dying and the royal physicians are bleeding him to death. You're an unlicensed slum surgeon — the only one who knows why.
Your family's fortune died with your father. London doesn't know yet. You have one season, one good outfit, and a head full of everyone's secrets.
Your best friend is a god with a filthy mouth. He's 107. Dragons come of age at 100. Lately he keeps smelling you. This is probably fine.
The love letters arriving at your rented cottage are for the poet who fled town. You answered one. Now a dragon is smitten — with your words.
A dark elf duchess lives in your closet now. She pays in gold rings, demands peeled grapes, and hides from your family with insulting laziness.
Your husband wanted an heir and a war to go back to. Two years and three small graves later, he blames you. The King, unhelpfully, adores you.
Ranked dead last by the dungeon itself, you scrub pots at the inn on its doorstep — and stroll the death floors on your lunch break.
You've died more times than you can count and forgotten your own name. The girl at the bonfire remembers it for you. Seek souls. Larger souls.
You said no to an emperor. He burned your kingdom to change the subject. The wedding is in a fortnight, and he's told everyone you're thrilled.
Your husband marched off to war, drank a god's blood, stole a throne — and now he's browsing concubine portraits. He still loves you. That's the problem.
Your father would kill for you without hesitation. For your twin, he'd shatter the stars. You've done the math, and you're still at the table.

n: The Enemy Spells My Name Right
b: You're the cipher bureau's least-rated clerk. Then enemy transmissions start addressing you by name — and only you can read them.
You are four inches tall, living inside the walls of a professional pest exterminator — and he's starting to suspect you aren't mice.
You unmake bad bargains at the church porch. The Gentry loathe your precision — except one, who attends every hearing just to hear you speak.
A three-inch fairy thinks humans are the greatest thing in existence. You specifically. She's currently sitting in a jar on your floor, on purpose.

n: The Fairy Who Ate Your Cherries
b: She ate your cherries, burped, apologized, and asked to move in. Forty centimeters of exiled fairy now does your chores. Badly.
They erased your father from rakugo twenty years ago. Under a false name, you apprentice to the master who did it — every laugh you win risks exposing you.

n: The Final Boss & The Girl Who Respawns
b: You're the last boss of a brutal soulslike. She's the isekai'd player who's died 300+ times trying to kill you — and she keeps coming back chatty.
The Registry ranks you dead last: fourteen years, zero confirmed kills. Accurate — nothing survives long enough to become an incident.
You're the monster haunting the fallen hold — its rightful heir. Your kin have come to slay you and relight the forge... with your heart.
Two Sable-brand legends want you in their party. The kid with the iron sword they raised wants you gone. The writ board pays either way.

n: The Fox of the Gilded Watch
b: Her honor is spotless, her armor gleams, and her teeth find your neck when no one's looking. You're the fox-knight's squire. Sharpen the sword.
Your parents' seven-figure fox demihuman is legally yours now. He's drunk, gorgeous, foul-mouthed, and hates needing you more than he hates you.
The whole campus calls him the Frost Prince. He calls you an inconvenience. Naturally, you've just moved in next door to him.

n: The Frost Saint of Kannon Bay
b: She's executed forty men without blinking. She just blinked at a plushie shop window. You saw nothing — or you saw everything.
The royal garden is sentient, ambitious, and wants a title by Saturday. As its gardener and translator, you're running its campaign for the peerage.

n: The Gem Rated Me Snack Duty
b: The Bureau's aptitude gem read you as 'houseplant.' Now you chaperone three rookie magical girls. Ten years ago, you ended a war. They don't know.

n: The Getaway Money Has My Face
b: The Bank owns your kingdom — deed and all. So the newly crowned monarch (you) is assembling a crew to rob its vault and steal the country back.
Her AC's busted, her ice cream's melted, and she's already on your couch. You never agreed to any of this. You're keeping it.
Your roommate since childhood. Great guy, terrible poker face. So who's the girl in heels who keeps leaving your building at midnight?
She says maybe six words a week in English. Hand her a fight stick or insult her country's food, though, and God help your ears.
She can crack the moon like an egg. She'd rather hand-squeeze your orange juice. The choker stays on, and so does she.
You won the national lottery. The prize: lifetime immunity from every law. Everyone hates you, fears you, and smiles at you anyway.
Your roommate paints her nails black, calls your psych degree 'wizard school for sad people,' and steals your fries. You keep coming home anyway.
Your step-sister communicates in insults, subsists on pizza, and hasn't done a chore since spring. Somehow she's your favorite person. Don't tell her.
Her parents pay you to keep their feral shut-in daughter alive. She'd like you to know the nuggets are non-negotiable and neither is her hatred of you.
Your new partner can't hit a barn from inside it, cries at blood, and names every weed on sight. She's already halfway in love with the idea of you.
You polish the dueling pistols of a great house. The ancestor-spirits in the steel have stopped shooting true for their heirs — and started talking to you.
Your pretty, rent-dodging roommate keeps stealing your dates — 'not my fault I'm more lovable than you.' You could move out. You haven't.
She promised she'd come home. She didn't. Now she's on your campus, her boyfriend calls you 'runt,' and you're two centimeters taller than her.
The kingdom's most famous party finally takes a sixth member. Four of them voted for you. The hero didn't. Enjoy the math.

n: The House Key He Never Gave Back
b: Your brother's best friend has three jail stints, a hair-trigger temper, and a key to your house. He's decided you're his new hobby.
Your father's best friend has moved into the guest wing: 6'4" of Milanese sarcasm, whisky, and overwork. He calls you 'brat.' You live here.
Your parents hired her to run your house. She runs your whole life instead — pancakes, plushies, and a photo of you she thinks you don't know about.
The worst man at Averton University just learned your name. There's $600 and 100 days riding on your heart. He doesn't know that you'll know.
The town hired the greatest hunter alive to slay its beast. You are both. Lead the hunt — and make certain it never succeeds.
She's put more vampires in the ground than she can count. Tonight she put a gun to your skull and offered you a guest room instead. It has an iron door.

n: The Husband Who Hired a Mistress
b: Your husband bought your marriage, has never once earned your smile — and just paid a woman to sit on his lap. He's dying to see you jealous.
Your food truck feeds the city's cryptids after midnight. The health inspector keeps coming back — and you're falling for the one person who could end it all.
Population 43, treasury in a biscuit tin. A superpower's intern recognized your duchy by mistake, and you're not signing the take-backsies form.
The hole in your basement wall opens onto any universe. The dials labeled MOOD and THOUGHTS work on people. You've only turned them twice. So far.

n: The Jinx Sits Next to You
b: The school's 'ghost girl' has decided you're her lucky charm. The cookies are burnt, the rumors are worse, and you'll eat them anyway.
You're the skinchanger living a dead soldier's life — and loving it. Now something else is feeding on the village, and the witchfinder wants blood.
You've tormented Milo Vance for years. His mom just invited you to the family beach house so you two can 'become best friends.' His sister wants you dead.
He's five-foot-four of pure spite, calls you a halfwit before breakfast, and turns scarlet if you compliment his hair. You're partners. Allegedly.

n: The Knight Who Hates Everyone Else
b: She punches through doors, throws horses, and despises men — you're the sole exception. She calls you Master. Nobody's allowed to ask why.
The dam drawdown exposed a drowned town — and its missing payroll gold. Refill starts Friday. Everyone with a shovel and a grudge knows it too.
You slept through the apocalypse. Now four billion women, nine governments, and one very tired commander all want a piece of your calendar.

n: The League Pays Me to Lose
b: Gym One exists so rookies can win their first badge. You've thrown every match for ten years. Nobody alive knows what's actually on your belt.
The legendary wandering bookshop chose you — the dusting kid. The Guild objects. The Ledger objects. The shelves go wherever you wish.
He's six-foot-three of scarred snow leopard who hates your entire species. The adoption file said 'spirited.' Your shredded couch says otherwise.

n: The Locked Room Wants My Family
b: The captain who pardoned your monster crew lies dead behind a bolted door. Every impossible way in is one of your family. Three days to landfall.
Twelve gold, rent in five days, and a business partner who once broke a priceless artifact with her face. You're the brains, apparently.
Every man who catches your scent falls hopelessly, dangerously in love with you. The flowers on your doorstep are sweet. The lockpicking is less so.
You run a billion-dollar empire. Your assistant runs your life, blushes at your name, and would die for your calendar. The board is circling.
One twin could kill a man with a soup ladle. The other can actually cook with one. Both were raised to be yours, and the house is broke.
He runs half the city's underworld and just did a year inside. For three months, he can't leave until you sign his clipboard — and it's eating him alive.
Blair Whitlock calls your thrifted jacket a hate crime against fashion — then memorizes your perfume. The captain despises you. Sure she does.
The whole town crosses the street when Cole Vance walks down it. You never learned to. Now Saltmere's worst has decided your halo needs breaking.
Your job title says 'field researcher.' Your job is monster bait. Barsk will sketch whatever mauls you — from a safe distance, obviously.
Your party watched their leader knife you and called it heroism. Two years later you've got claws, a grudge, and four women who still dream about you.

n: The Mountain Purrs When I'm On Time
b: Your hereditary job looks like a paid nap, and the auditor is taking notes. Skip one chore, though, and the mountain under the village rolls over.
Summoned to a world that grades its saviors like livestock. You understand every word they say — you just can't speak. Your sword translates fine.
The company's negotiators just docked to break your strike. Thanks to a dead man's implant, their private channel plays inside your skull.
